title: WCLI-98 follow-up: the refused-header detail is dropped by reporting.ts and profiles.ts, and no test drives it to stderr
description: From the Opus review of ward-cli#215 at a513c52 (finding 5). reporting.ts:85-87 and :249-252 and profiles.ts:210-214 catch the profile refusal and drop the refusedHeader detail, so the name is not printed on those paths. Both fail safe and leak nothing. Suggestion: a runWard test drives a refused name to stderr and asserts the canonical suffix there. Not built in ward-cli#215.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each path that catches a profile refusal either carries the canonical refusedHeader detail or is shown to need none
A runWard test drives a refused header name to stderr and asserts the canonical suffix and that no declared byte is printed

implementationNotes: Built on feat/wcli-116-refused-header-detail-cli as test/refused-header-cli.test.ts, no source change. Finding: the paths that print an error (profile approve, run) already carry the canonical suffix; the paths that catch the refusal (profiles.ts:210-214 for profile list and check; reporting.ts:85-87 and :249-252 for status and doctor) report an enumerated state ("declaration": "invalid", reasons ["declaration"], binding unknown, state_malformed) with no free-text field, so there is no place for a name and none is added. 15 runWard cases: approve and run print "(refused header: <canonical>)" and never the declared spelling or any value; list, check, status and doctor print their state and neither the declared name, the canonical name, nor a value; an unlisted header is never printed on any path. Mutation controls: dropping the suffix and echoing the declared name each reddened exactly the 6 approve and run cases. No reporting-path mutation was run, since those paths have no detail channel to mutate. Whether status and doctor should name the header is a design question, not decided here. Acceptance criteria left unchecked pending review.
